difficultyAxis: Layering trap through prefix-colliding names: Shipment, ShipmentItem and ShipmentItemAdjustment form a child-of-child chain whose class names nest, alongside a second independent reference chain (Warehouse, Carrier) into the same aggregate. The tempting mistake is to collapse the three Shipment* classes into one controller or to inject one service into another instead of keeping one repository per entity and resolving references in the service.
rationale: Six entities, fifteen scenarios and a three-level reference path (ShipmentItemAdjustment -> ShipmentItem -> Shipment -> Warehouse/Carrier). The names are chosen so that a generator keying on the longest common prefix, or one that derives a service by stripping a suffix, produces a wrong module boundary. Unhappy paths assert service-level rejection of a missing reference, which cannot be satisfied by bean validation alone.

userStories.intent: register a warehouse with a region and a capacity
userStories.benefit: shipments can be dispatched from a known facility

scenarios.given: a unique warehouse code and a positive capacity
scenarios.then: the warehouse is persisted and returned with its generated identifier

scenarios.given: a capacity of zero or less
scenarios.when: the operator attempts to register the warehouse
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid before reaching the service layer

userStories.intent: register a carrier with a service level
userStories.benefit: shipments are assigned to a compliant transport provider

scenarios.given: a carrier code matching the permitted pattern and a service level
scenarios.then: the carrier is persisted and returned with its generated identifier

scenarios.given: a carrier code that does not match the permitted pattern
scenarios.when: the planner attempts to register the carrier
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: dispatch a shipment from a warehouse through a carrier
userStories.benefit: goods leave the facility under a tracked reference

scenarios.given: an existing warehouse, an existing carrier and a positive total weight
scenarios.then: the shipment is persisted with its warehouse and carrier references intact

scenarios.given: a shipment referencing a warehouse identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the dispatcher attempts to create the shipment
scenarios.then: the service rejects the shipment and reports the missing warehouse reference

scenarios.given: a total weight below the permitted minimum
scenarios.when: the dispatcher attempts to create the shipment
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: add packing items to a dispatched shipment
userStories.benefit: the shipment contents and declared value are auditable

scenarios.given: an existing shipment and a quantity within the permitted range
scenarios.then: the item is persisted against the shipment and returned with its identifier

scenarios.given: a shipment identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the dispatcher attempts to add an item to it
scenarios.then: the service reports the shipment as not found

scenarios.given: a quantity above the permitted maximum
scenarios.when: the dispatcher attempts to add the item
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: apply a monetary adjustment to a packing item
userStories.benefit: the billed value of the item reflects the correction

scenarios.given: an existing shipment item and a positive adjustment amount
scenarios.then: the adjustment is persisted against the item with its reason code and author

scenarios.given: a shipment item identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the controller attempts to apply the adjustment
scenarios.then: the service reports the shipment item as not found

userStories.intent: record tracking events against a shipment in occurrence order
userStories.benefit: the customer-facing timeline reflects what actually happened

scenarios.given: an existing shipment and an occurrence time in the past
scenarios.when: the operator records the tracking event
scenarios.then: the event is persisted against the shipment with its occurrence time

scenarios.given: an occurrence time in the future
scenarios.when: the operator attempts to record the event
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: read the packing items of one shipment
userStories.benefit: the manifest can be reviewed before departure

scenarios.given: a shipment with no packing items
scenarios.when: the dispatcher reads the items for that shipment
scenarios.then: the service returns an empty collection rather than reporting an error
